stem: Where does a dashboard component get its data?

options.text: From a source report
Directly from an object
From a page layout
From a permission set

explanation: Every component is built from a report. You must create the report before the component.

stem: How many source reports can one dashboard component use?

options.text: One
Two
Up to five
Unlimited

explanation: Each component is based on exactly one source report. Use several components for several reports.

stem: What is the maximum number of components on one dashboard?
explanation: A dashboard can have up to 20 components.

stem: Which component shows one number measured against a target with coloured ranges?

options.text: Gauge
Metric
Table
Funnel chart

explanation: A gauge shows a value against a target and uses colour bands such as red, yellow and green.

stem: Which component shows a single large number, such as total open pipeline?

options.text: Metric
Gauge
Chart
Table

explanation: A metric displays one number without a scale or target.

stem: Which component is best for showing the top five open deals as a ranked list?

options.text: Table
Gauge
Metric
Donut chart

explanation: A table lists records in rows, which suits a short ranked list.

stem: Which component is best for comparing pipeline across stages?

options.text: Chart
Metric
Gauge
Table of notes

explanation: Charts such as bar and column compare groups. Metrics and gauges show one number.

stem: What does the running user of a dashboard decide?

options.text: Whose data access determines what everyone sees on the dashboard
Who is allowed to edit the dashboard and its components
Which folder the dashboard is stored in and shared from
How often the dashboard refreshes its data each day

explanation: The dashboard runs its reports as the running user, so viewers see that person's view of the data.

stem: The running user of a dashboard is the CEO, who can see all records. What do regional managers who open it see?

options.text: The CEO's view of the data, including records they cannot normally see
Only the data of their own region
Nothing, because they need CEO permissions to open it
An error, because the dashboard is set to run as the CEO

explanation: Viewers see what the running user can see. To restrict by viewer, use a dynamic dashboard.

stem: Each regional manager must see only the data they are allowed to see on one shared dashboard. What should the admin use?

options.text: A dynamic dashboard, run as the logged-in user
A dashboard with the CEO as running user
A joined report
A reporting snapshot

explanation: A dynamic dashboard runs as the person viewing it, so everyone sees their own data.

stem: Which statement about dynamic dashboards is true?

options.text: They cannot be scheduled to refresh
They can be scheduled to refresh daily
They cannot be viewed by managers
They always run as the CEO

explanation: Viewers refresh dynamic dashboards manually. Dashboards with a specific running user can be scheduled.

stem: The sales director wants the same figures emailed to the team every Monday morning, refreshed automatically. Which setup fits?

options.text: A dashboard with a specific running user, scheduled and subscribed
A dynamic dashboard that shows each viewer their own data
A joined report that is emailed to the team
A matrix report that is sent without a dashboard

explanation: Only dashboards with a specific running user can be scheduled to refresh and then sent through subscriptions.

stem: How many filters can a dashboard have?

options.text: Three
One
Five
Ten

explanation: A dashboard supports up to three filters, which update all components.

stem: A dashboard is used to:

options.text: View data from reports visually, without editing it
Entering and editing records on the dashboard page
Defining validation rules for the reports behind it
Importing data from files into Salesforce

explanation: Dashboards are read-only views of report data.

objective: Explain who can see a dashboard
stem: A user can open the dashboard folder but not the folder holding its source report. What can they do?

options.text: View the dashboard but not open the underlying report
Nothing, because the folders are unrelated
Edit the source report behind the dashboard
View the report but not the dashboard

explanation: Dashboard folder access lets them see the dashboard. Opening the source report needs access to its folder.

stem: A manager says the dashboard numbers look wrong. In what order should the admin check?

options.text: Running user, source report filters, last refresh time
Page layout, record types, profile of the manager
Validation rules, flows, apps used by the team
Recycle Bin, merge history, mass delete log

explanation: These three explain most complaints: who the dashboard runs as, what the report is filtered to, and how old the data is.

stem: Which TWO statements about dynamic dashboards are true? (Choose 2)

options.text: Each viewer sees data based on their own access
They cannot be scheduled to refresh
Everyone sees the same figures
They can use joined reports as sources

explanation: Dynamic dashboards run as the viewer and must be refreshed manually. They do not give everyone identical figures, and joined reports are never valid sources.

stem: Which of these can be used directly as the data source of a dashboard component?

options.text: A report
An object
A permission set
A page layout

explanation: Components use reports. Build the report first, then add the component.

stem: What is a good first step when designing a new dashboard?

options.text: Decide what question and decision the audience needs it for
Add all 20 components first and remove the ones you do not need
Choose the brightest colours to make the dashboard stand out
Pick the running user last, without testing what they see

explanation: Start from the audience and the decision. A focused dashboard of five to eight components is more useful than a crowded one.

stem: Which of the following best describes a dashboard filter?

options.text: A control that lets viewers narrow all components, for example by owner
A filter that sits inside one report and changes only that report
A security setting that restricts which users can open the dashboard
A way to hide the dashboard from users who do not need it

explanation: Dashboard filters change all components at once, within the limit of three filters.

objective: Explain who can see a dashboard
stem: Who decides which folders a dashboard can be viewed from?

options.text: The folder's sharing settings (Viewer, Editor, Manager)
The page layout assigned to the dashboard tab
The record type of the report behind each component
The validation rule on the running user's profile

explanation: Dashboards live in folders, and folder sharing controls who can open or edit them.

stem: A dashboard component needs a chart of opportunities grouped by stage. Which source report format is most suitable?

options.text: Summary
Joined
A report with no grouping and no row limit
A report with no records

explanation: Charts need grouped data, so a summary or matrix report is the right source. Joined reports cannot be sources.

stem: Each sales rep should see only their own numbers on the same dashboard. Which setting fits?

options.text: Run as the logged-in user
Run as a specified manager
A public folder only
A dashboard subscription

explanation: Dynamic dashboards run as the viewer, so each person sees data they are allowed to see.
